DEEPREVIEW_ICML2025.argument: This paper proposes the Pose Prior Learner (PPL) for unsupervised pose estimation.
It learns a categorical pose prior and uses a hierarchical memory to store prototypical poses.
The model can be used for pose estimation even in occluded scenes through iterative inference.
Experiments show that PPL outperforms existing methods across several pose estimation benchmarks.
PPL introduces a new method for unsupervised pose estimation by learning pose priors, which is a novel approach in the field.
The authors conducted experiments on several benchmarks and showed that PPL outperforms existing methods.
The iterative inference strategy also allows for pose estimation in occluded scenes.
The method seems to be limited to 2D pose estimation, which may not be suitable for scenarios involving 3D postures.
The lack of explicit 3D modeling limits its applicability in scenarios where depth information is crucial, such as in robotics or augmented reality applications where accurate 3D pose is necessary.
The performance of PPL may degrade when objects undergo significant rotations or shape changes.

The reliance on a learned pose prior might not generalize well to unseen poses or object configurations, especially when the observed pose deviates significantly from the training data's distribution.
This could be due to the method's inability to handle large discontinuities in the pose space.
The authors did not discuss how to determine the number of memory banks and vectors in each memory bank.
The lack of a principled approach for setting these hyperparameters makes the method difficult to reproduce and adapt to new datasets.
The paper should provide more guidance on how to choose these values based on the characteristics of the data.
